record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.context_brief: Finite-element convergence for quasi-isometric variational maps
record.original_question: For the quasi-isometric variational principle whose feasible condition is det grad y > t Phi(det grad y, grad y) almost everywhere with t>0, for which broad classes of boundary data and solutions can one prove global uniqueness of the minimizer and convergence of finite-element approximations, beyond the smooth near-identity regime where an implicit-function-theorem argument is expected to apply?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega, \Omega^* \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) be bounded Lipschitz domains, and let $y:\Omega \to \Omega^*$ be a mapping in a suitable Sobolev space $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)$ subject to prescribed boundary data $y|_{\partial\Omega} = y_0$. Consider a quasi-isometric variational principle in which one minimizes a polyconvex stored-energy functional
$$ I[y] = \int_\Omega F(\nabla y, \det \nabla y)\, dx $$
over the admissible class
$$ \mathcal{A}_t = \{\, y \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d) : y|_{\partial\Omega} = y_0,\ \det \nabla y(x) > t\,\Phi(\det \nabla y(x), \nabla y(x)) \text{ a.e. in } \Omega \,\}, $$
where $t > 0$ is a fixed parameter and $\Phi:\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^{d\times d} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is a continuous function chosen so that the constraint guarantees a uniform bilipschitz (quasi-isometry) bound on $y$ with a constant depending only on $t$.

For this constrained variational problem, identify broad classes of admissible boundary data $y_0$ and corresponding minimizers $y^*$ for which one can rigorously establish:
(a) global uniqueness of the minimizer of $I$ over $\mathcal{A}_t$, and
(b) convergence (in an appropriate norm, with explicit rates if possible) of conforming finite-element approximations $y_h^*$ minimizing the discretized functional over a piecewise-polynomial subspace of $\mathcal{A}_t$, as the mesh size $h \to 0$,

beyond the regime of smooth boundary data with near-identity solutions, where uniqueness and convergence follow from a standard implicit-function-theorem perturbation argument.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that convergence of iterations to stationary points has been proven for polyconvex and quasi-isometric functionals, and existence/uniqueness has been studied for restricted problems (volume and smoothness), but a general global-uniqueness and finite-element-convergence theory beyond the near-identity / smooth regime does not appear to have been established. The question is posed explicitly as an open problem and no subsequent work clearly resolving it was found.

status_evidence.title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling
status_evidence.snippet: attempts to formulate general requirements which should be satisfied by the variational principle... open problems
status_evidence.claim: The question is identified as part of an open-problem list.

status_evidence.title: Barrier variational generation of quasi-isometric grids
status_evidence.snippet: convergence of iterations to a stationary point of the discrete functional was rigorously proven for the most known polyconvex stored energies and for a quasi-isometric functional
status_evidence.claim: Only convergence to stationary points (not global uniqueness or FE convergence of minimizers) is known.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical aspects of variational grid generation II
status_evidence.snippet: existence and uniqueness of solutions of the volume and smoothness problems
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness results exist only for restricted subproblems, not for the general quasi-isometric variational principle.
